## Submission 1

```{r}

## need to switch X (ProbeID) and geoID in expression data 
## want to save the X column data 
X <- expData$X
## first - need to make ProbeID/X the row names 
## want to keep X attached to its corresponding data
rownames(expData) <- expData$X
#head(expData)
## then need to delete the X column because it is now the row names 
expData <- expData[ , -1]
#head(expData)
## then transpose the data - so the rows become columns/columns become rows
expData_t <- as.data.frame(t(expData))
#head(expData_t)
## lost the X so i can restore 
#colnames(expData_t) <- X
#head(expData_t)

## change the probeID to gene name in the merged sheet 
# ?match()
names(expData_t) <- namesData$GENE[match(names(expData_t), namesData$PROBEID)]
#head(expData_t)

## need to add a geoID label on the first cell of the sheet 
expData_t$geoID <- rownames(expData_t)
#head(expData_t)

## can then merge data on geoID variable 
merged <- merge(covarData, expData_t, by = "geoID")

```


```{r}

## All submitted plots must be made using ggplot2 and must be of publication quality
## Identify one gene, one continuous covariate, and two categorical covariates of interest. 
## At least one categorical variable should be derived from a continuous variable
## gene - NPPB 
## one continuous covariate - mat_age_years
## two categorical covariates, one must be derived - 
## preg_preclampsia, mat_vitD_group 

# class(merged$mat_vitD) - its chr - will need to change to numeric so i can group
# head(merged$mat_vitD) - contains a string before the numbers - will need to remove
## substitute everything up to : with "" empty space in the mat_vitD variable from merged
merged$mat_vitD <- as.numeric(sub(".*:", "", merged$mat_vitD))

## then subset into groups for the derived categorical variable from a continuous
## low = <30; high = >=30
merged$mat_vitD_group <- ifelse(merged$mat_vitD <30, "Insufficient (<30 ng/mL)", 
                                "Sufficient (≥30 ng/mL)")

#class(merged$mat_age_yrs) # is chr - need to change to numeric 
## can use same format as vitamin d 
merged$mat_age_yrs <- as.numeric(sub(".*:", "", merged$mat_age_yrs))
#head(merged$mat_age_yrs)

# head(merged$preg_preeclampsia) - need to change to normal and preclampsia only 
## use sub 
merged$preg_preeclampsia <- sub(".*:", "", merged$preg_preeclampsia)
#head(merged$preg_preeclampsia)
```

```{r}

## define a nice theme for my plots 

my_theme <- theme(
        # Remove all the extra borders and grid lines
        panel.border = element_blank(), panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), 
        # Define  axis
        axis.line = element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = rel(1)),
        # Set plot background
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
        panel.background = element_blank(),
        legend.key = element_rect(fill = 'white'), 
        # Move legend
        legend.position = 'top', 
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

```

## Submission 2 
Identify 2 additional genes (3 total)
- MYL2
- PLN 
Build a function that produces the plots for submission 1 above. 
  - Your function should loop through all genes provided to it to produce the plots from your first submission (including 1 continuous covariate and 2 categorical covariates). 

```{r}

# function for building - Histogram of Gene Expression
fun_hist <- function(df, gene) {
  # [[]] to select the value of the gene expression within the columns
  ggplot(df, aes(df[[gene]])) +
  geom_histogram(fill = "blue", color = "black") +
  labs(title = bquote("Histogram of " *italic(.(gene))* " Gene Expression"), x = "Gene Expression",
       y = "Frequency") +
  my_theme
}

# function for building - Scatterplot of Covariate vs. Gene Expression
fun_scatter <- function(df, x, gene){
  ggplot(df, aes(x = df[[x]], y = df[[gene]], color = df[[x]]))+ 
  geom_point()+
  labs(title = bquote("Maternal Age vs " *italic(.(gene))* " Gene Expression"), x = "Maternal Age (Years)", 
       y = bquote(italic(.(gene))* " Gene Expression"), 
       color = "Maternal Age (Years)") +
  my_theme 
}

# function for building - Boxplot of Gene Expression Separated by Both Categorical Variables
fun_box <- function(df, x, gene) {
  set.seed(4)
  ggplot(df, aes(x = df[[x]],  y = df[[gene]], color = mat_vitD_group)) +
    geom_boxplot()+
    geom_jitter (position = position_jitterdodge())+
    labs(title = bquote(italic(.(gene))* " Gene Expression by Preeclampsia and Vitamin D Group"), 
         x = "Pregnancy Condition", y = bquote(italic(.(gene))* " Gene Expression"), color = "Vitamin D Level") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("orange", "blue")) +
    my_theme 
}

```


```{r}
# revision based on feedback from submission 2 
# list of genes to loop through 
geneList <- c("NPPB", "MYL2", "PLN")

allPlots2 <- function(merged, geneList) {
  for(i in 1:length(geneList)) {
    print(fun_hist(merged, geneList[i]))
    
    print(fun_scatter(merged, "mat_age_yrs", geneList[i]))
    
    print(fun_box(merged, "preg_preeclampsia", geneList[i]))
  
  }
}

allPlots2(merged, geneList)

```


## Final Submission 

Your final project should be submitted as a formatted LaTeX document with the following sections:
Methods 
•	Describe and cite the data source including initial sample size
•	Final sample size and justification for removing any data points (if applicable) 
•	Describe any analyses conducted
•	Cite software and packages (and versions used)
•	Link GitHub repository
Results 
•	Description of the findings of each table/figure (outlined below). For each item, provide a brief statement referencing and interpreting them and then cite the relevant table or figure, as discussed in class. Example: “Gene x was not associated with covariate y (Figure 2).” All items must be typeset with captions/figure legends as discussed in class. 
•	Summary statistics table (LaTeX formatted) with all covariates you looked at and 2 additional continuous covariates (3 continuous, 2 categorical total), stratified a categorical covariate
•	Publication quality plots from submission 2 (incorporating any previous feedback)
•	Publication quality heatmap (10 genes, tracking bars for 2 categorical variables, clustering)
•	One additional plot type not previously discussed in class to visualize your data in a new and unique way. Be creative! See list at end of document for plot types that would not count. 
References
At a minimum, your references must include the original paper that the dataset came from and any R packages used. All references should be cited within the text as shown in class.

```{r}
# 1 Heatmap - 10 genes, tracking bars for 2 categorical variables, clustering
# already chosen genes: NPPB, MYL2, PLN 
# 7 additional: 
# NKX2-5, TBX20, CRYAB, AKAP6, PDE2A, CDH2, ACTG2 
#install.packages("pheatmap")
library(pheatmap)

# extract and transpose the genes of interest
genes_heat_df <- t(merged[ , c("NPPB", "MYL2", "PLN", "NKX2-5", "TBX20", "CRYAB", "AKAP6", 
                  "PDE2A", "CDH2", "ACTG2")])
colnames(genes_heat_df) <- rownames(merged)

# for tracking bar
# follow notes from 06 data analytics class 

set.seed(4)
annotationData2 <- data.frame(row.names = colnames(genes_heat_df), 
                              "preg_preeclampsia" = factor(merged$preg_preeclampsia),
                              "mat_vitD_group" = factor(merged$mat_vitD_group))
colnames(annotationData2) <- c("Pregnancy Status", "Maternal Vitamin D Group")

annotationColors <- list(`Pregnancy Status`= c(" Preeclampsia" = "pink", 
                                          " Normal" = "purple"), 
                         `Maternal Vitamin D Group` = c("Insufficient (<30 ng/mL)" = "orange", 
                                      "Sufficient (≥30 ng/mL)" = "blue"))

# remove the participant id - its clustered together and not presentation ready 
pheatmap(genes_heat_df,
         clustering_distance_cols = 'euclidean',
         clustering_distance_rows = 'euclidean',
         annotation_col = annotationData2,
         annotation_colors = annotationColors, 
         cluster_cols = T, 
         cluster_rows = T,
         clustering_method = "complete",
         main = "Gene Expression Heatmap", 
         show_colnames = F)

```


```{r}
# 1 Additional Plot (See Below) - The following plots types would not count towards 
# the “additional plot” for the final submission:
# Scatter plots, Histograms, Density plots, Violin plots, Correlation plots, Heatmaps

# i want to examine how the 10 gene expression levels vary by preeclampsia status
# utilize circular bar plot -  uses coord_polar() within ggplot2 

# create list to of genes to find means of - 10 genes used in heatmap
geneList2 <- merged[ , c("NPPB", "MYL2", "PLN", "NKX2-5", "TBX20", "CRYAB", "AKAP6", 
                  "PDE2A", "CDH2", "ACTG2")]

gene_means <- colMeans(geneList2)
#print(gene_means)

gene_means_df <- data.frame(Gene = names(gene_means), 
                            mean_exp = gene_means)
#View(gene_means_df)

# now create plot with gene means df
# want to color by the genes 
#?theme()
# geom_col to plot the mean values from df 
ggplot(gene_means_df, aes(x = Gene, y = mean_exp, fill = Gene)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_polar() + 
  labs(title = "Mean Gene Expression") +
  # need to clean up the plot 
  # remove the x and y axis, the ticks, and numbers 
  # need to make gene names smaller so they dont get cut off 
  theme(axis.title = element_blank(), 
        axis.ticks = element_blank(), 
        axis.line.x.bottom = element_blank(), 
        axis.line.y = element_blank(), 
        axis.text.y = element_blank(), 
        axis.text = element_text(size = 7.5)) +
  my_theme

```
